user.title: Set up CSNet Home
user.description: Enter your CSNet Manager credentials to connect your Hitachi system to Home Assistant.

data.energy_meter: Electricity meter of the heat pump (optional)
data.energy_meter_power: Power sensor of the heat pump (optional)

data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll for updates (default: 60 seconds)
data_description.language: Preferred language for device names and alarms
data_description.card_language: Automatic follows each user's Home Assistant profile. A card can still set its own language.
data_description.max_temp_override: Override the maximum temperature limit (8-80°C). Leave empty for defaults.
data_description.fan_coil_model: Select the fan coil control type (standard or legacy)
data_description.always_offer_dhw_boost: Enables the boost mode for domestic hot water on units where it is not available.
data_description.power_supply: Used to estimate instant power and COP. Auto detects 8/10 HP units as three phase, others as single phase.
data_description.enable_alarm_notifications: Create a Home Assistant notification when the unit reports an alarm
data_description.filtered_alarm_codes: Comma-separated alarm codes that never notify (default: -1, communication errors). Leave empty to notify all.
data_description.energy_meter: Any energy sensor (kWh) that measures the heat pump's electricity, from any device. Used to compute the COP from the heat CSNet records. Leave empty to keep the estimate only.
data_description.energy_meter_power: The power sensor (W or kW) that goes with the electricity meter, for Instant Consumption. With a three-phase meter, choose the total of the phases, or a helper that adds them up. Leave empty to use the power sensor found on the meter's device.
data_description.heat_source: Where the heat produced comes from, for every accumulated heating, cooling and hot water counter and every daily or period COP. CSNet: the heat CSNet Manager records for the unit (by full hours). Calculated: the integration's own measure, from the water flow and the exchanger's temperatures, in real time. With CSNet, the integration's measure is used when CSNet has not recorded any heat for the unit. Automatic: CSNet's heat, hour by hour, and the integration's measure for the hours CSNet has no record for or recorded less than half of it.
data_description.user_agent: How the integration presents itself to CSNet Manager. Leave empty to use the default (a desktop Chrome browser). Change it only to test another value.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure CSNet Home
reconfigure.description: Update your CSNet Home configuration. Leave the password empty to keep the current one.

heating_curves.title: Heating curves
heating_curves.description: CSNet reports the kind of heating curve (water law) each circuit uses ({circuits}) but not its values. Copy the values your installer set on the unit controller (Space heating > Water calculation mode). They are only used to compute the heating curve water temperature sensors: nothing is sent to the unit. Leave a circuit empty to have no sensor for it.

recalculate_cop.title: Recalculate past COPs
recalculate_cop.description:
The COPs from {first} to {last}, worked out again from Home Assistant's statistics: the heat of the integration's calculated heat power ({heat}) over the electricity your meter counted ({meter}). Nothing is sent to the unit.

| Day | Heat (kWh) | Electricity (kWh) | COP before | Recalculated COP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
{table}

"COP before" is what COP today showed at the end of the day. Confirming rewrites {hours} hourly statistics of {sensors}: the history graphs and statistics show the recalculated values. The recorded states of the last days do not change. The values replaced are kept: this menu can put them back.

restore_cop.title: Put back the COPs as they were
restore_cop.description: Puts back the {hours} hourly statistics of the COP sensors that the recalculation replaced, as they were before it.

error.incomplete_curve: Fill in every value of this circuit's curve, or none of them.
error.high_ambient_not_above_low: The high ambient temperature must be above the low ambient temperature.

abort.not_loaded: The integration must be loaded to read which heating curves the unit uses. Try again once it has started.
abort.no_heating_curve: None of the circuits uses a points or gradient heating curve, so there is nothing to describe. A fixed water temperature already has its own entity.
abort.no_recorder: The recalculation reads Home Assistant's statistics, and the recorder is not running.
abort.no_energy_meter: The recalculation divides by what your electricity meter counted. Choose the heat pump's electricity meter in the integration's settings (Reconfigure) first.
abort.no_cop_sensors: The heat power sensor or the COP sensors were not found.
abort.no_statistics: Home Assistant has no hourly statistics with both the heat power and the electricity meter yet.
abort.cop_history_unchanged: The COPs in the statistics already match the recalculation: nothing to change.
abort.cop_history_recalculated: {hours} hourly statistics of the COP sensors rewritten. Graphs may need a reload of the page to show them.
abort.cop_history_restored: {hours} hourly statistics of the COP sensors put back as they were.
abort.no_cop_backup: There is nothing to put back.

options.auto: Automatic: CSNet, calculated where CSNet missed hours
